newsitem.title: UK: RTZ-CRA Q3 copper mine output up 9.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: RTZ-CRA Q3 copper mine output up 9.0 pct.

text.p: Mining group RTZ-CRA said on Thursday that production in the third quarter of 1996 was up on the 1995 period for almost all its products and total copper mine output rose nine percent.

The Anglo-Australian company said that the Escondida Phase III expansion in Chile had increased its copper output by 63 percent and that this offset the effect of lower ore grades at Bingham Canyon in the U.S.
Total refined copper output rose by 48 percent.
U.S. coal production was six percent higher following increased demanded for low sulphur coal from the Antelope, Colowyo and Spring Creek sites.
Industrial action hit Australian coal output but this was partially offset by improvements at Kaltim Prima in Indonesia.
Increased output at Bell Bay in Australia and the smelter expansion project at New Zealand's Tiwai Point boosted Comalco's aluminium production by 11 per cent.
Titanium dioxide feedstock production was 14 per cent higher while borates output increased by five per cent.
First production was recorded for the re-opened Greens Creek U.S. mine -- 465,000 ounces silver, 1,720 tonnes zinc, 820 tonnes lead and approximately 1,000 ounces of gold.

On June 30, the group provisionally priced 202,000 tonnes (445 million lbs) of sales of copper in concentrate or matte at an average of $1,984/tonne (90c/lb). On September 30, it priced a further 217,000 tonnes (478 million lbs) at the same level.
Additionally, 75,000 tonnes of copper from Bingham Canyon remained unsold on 30 September. This is a 5,000 tonne increase since June 30, resulting from higher production.
The stockpile will be reduced as smelter performance and fourth quarter concentrate sales volumes improve, it said.
